operations.comment: ; RAM aliases describe the active consumer, not exclusive ownership of an address.
; SourcePointer ($86/$87), SecondPointer ($88/$89) and ResultPointer ($8A/$8B)
; are shared scratch pairs: copy/PPU inputs, decimal operands, and temporary arithmetic.
; WorkCount/WorkIndex/ScratchOne..Three are freely reused counters and temporaries.
; BallDirection and following fields name the primary working record only; indexed
; accesses may address the swapped secondary records. Enemy fields are parallel arrays.
; SoundWorkPointer ($E6/$E7) also holds command indices and arithmetic intermediates;
; APURegisterZero ($EB) doubles as the channel-iteration limit before APU rendering.
; Physical data labels identify storage positions; names ending CPU are fixed CPU views.
; Named table bases plus offsets preserve known consumers without asserting subtable extents.
; ROMAtlas NES commentary; all assets remain local.
; Fixed 32 KiB PRG: CPU $8000/$A000/$C000/$E000 use physical 8 KiB banks [0,1,2,3].
; CNROM writes select CHR only. CPU RAM, PPU addresses and physical ROM offsets are distinct.
; Ball working record: 26 bytes at $33, with copies at +$1A and +$34.
; Enemy fields are parallel three-byte arrays; OAM entries are Y,tile,attributes,X.
; SourcePointer/SecondPointer/ResultPointer also serve decimal arithmetic operands.
; iNES header: mapper 3, 32 KiB fixed PRG, 16 KiB CHR, horizontal mirroring, no trainer.

; Disable interrupts/rendering, wait three vblanks, clear scratch RAM and establish the stack. Preserve the high-score/threshold area when its warm-boot signature matches; player score RAM is cleared on either path. Initialize the frame-driven game and park in the foreground loop. All gameplay runs inside NMI.
; The PPU status read acknowledges vblank; wait for each fresh sample before continuing reset.
; A signature mismatch replaces all twelve signature/high-score bytes; matching startup retains them. Both paths subsequently clear player scores and remaining score work RAM.
; Foreground remains here; the NMI scheduler owns all ongoing game work.
; Unknown physical $009E / CPU $808E: isolated $60, between reset idle loop and signature.
; No supported entry, fetch or consumer establishes code versus data. Preserve this byte without decoding.
; Twelve-byte warm-boot signature compared and copied by Reset; only the first six bytes are checked.
; Maskable interrupts are not used by this program; return without work.
; Three non-code bytes between IRQ return and NMI entry; no specific field meaning is established.

; Commit scroll/control shadows and DMA the previous OAM buffer. Unless the frame hold is active, service gameplay/display/input in this fixed order; sound and timers always run. Registers are scratch: foreground never resumes meaningful computation.
; The frame hold skips game work but still runs sound, timer decrement and final scroll/control commits.
; Accept a new A press or the READY timeout, clear attachment/pause bookkeeping and enter active play with a launch sound.

; Ignore movement while inactive, paused, dying or escaping. Convert paddle-controller position or left/right buttons to a signed delta, clip the six paddle pieces to the arena, and move an attached ball by the same delta.
; Return a caught ball to the READY state and arm its automatic release timer.
; Intersect capsule and paddle bounds. Consume the capsule once, queue its points and dispatch seven effects: slow, catch, expand, multiball, laser, escape or extra life.
; Lower speed indices without allowing zero, synchronize speed fields and restart the motion script.

; Choose the first eligible destroyed brick, derive its screen position, mix game state to choose a capsule, avoid the previous type and select its eight-byte animation stream. Some choices differ in attract mode.

; Capsule selection exceptions followed by eight-byte tile animation streams. SpawnCapsuleFromBrick chooses a type; UpdateCapsuleSprite treats $FF as wrap. The entire block is data; subtable boundaries follow those consumers.
; For each changed brick, update or allocate one of six four-byte animation slots. Run their frame/timer sequence into pairs of OAM sprites; a zero tile pair frees the slot.
; Match a brick position against six existing animation records, or allocate a free record for a qualifying hit.
; Advance active animation records at three-frame intervals and copy their Y/X positions and paired tile indices to OAM.
; Six pairs of tiles for brick-hit animation phases. A zero first tile terminates and frees the animation slot.
; When the escape power is armed and the paddle reaches the right boundary, stop balls and lasers, award points and animate all six paddle pieces offscreen.
; Six unpacked decimal digits queued when entering the escape gate.
; A new Start edge pauses active play. Resumption requires the matching button transition count and queues the pause-message refresh; attract mode ignores this path.
; Wait for pending points before deciding whether a cleared playfield advances the stage or loss of all balls consumes a life. Preserve the surviving ball record when collapsing multiball.
; Copy a surviving 26-byte ball record to the primary slot and retain only its active bit.
; Freeze timers in pause. Frame hold gates the scheduler; otherwise advance attract/menu timeouts, capsule/laser/READY timers and the timed boss/ending state transitions.
; Advance the timed state, or reset attract mode on its terminal states. The story/attract setup seeds a fresh two-byte timer.
; Resolve boss death, story delay and ending-return delays through explicit main-state transitions.
; On a new A press allocate either of two laser pairs with a short firing cooldown, then move them upward. Remove each pair on arena exit or a brick collision.
; Convert laser Y/X to the 8-by-16 brick grid. Test the two horizontally overlapped cells, apply each hit and return carry when either was occupied.
; Test both active laser pairs against roaming enemy rectangles; consume a pair when it destroys an enemy.
; Search three active emerged enemies for overlap with the supplied laser position, queue score and start the matched enemy explosion. Carry reports a hit.
; Overlap the paddle rectangle with three active enemies, award collision points and start their explosion sequences.

; Sequence paddle collapse, tile changes and an eighteen-sprite explosion with delays. Save the current player lives/brick timers, alternate players when appropriate, then initialize another round or enter game over.
; Save player-specific counters and timers before deciding on player alternation or game over.
; Two consecutive eighteen-tile paddle explosion frames, indexed while composing eighteen OAM entries.
; Increment current stage and its decimal display digits. Save the current player lives/stage, clear remaining-brick state and request staged initialization after a short hold.
; Latch both controller ports and preserve previous samples for edge tests. Also shift the paddle peripheral bits, normalize its position and select the active player button sample.
; Upload the complete 256-byte sprite buffer at CPU RAM $0200 to OAM.
; In READY or active play, flush changed brick tiles. Defer other PPU work while a new capsule palette needs upload; otherwise update lives, escape gate, enemy hatch, player blink and score display.
; Outside attract mode, alternate the active player label and blanks every thirty frames, restoring the PPU mask after the write.

; Consume three-byte PPU-update records, write each two-tile brick pair, reset the no-hit timer and decrement the remaining-brick count only for removal records. Pick the hit/destruction sound from the final record.
; Queue points from changed bricks, then drain a six-digit pending decimal amount into the active score. Compare against high score and award threshold lives; attract mode does not add points.
; Two six-digit decimal amounts used to drain pending points and award enemy/capsule points. Source selection depends on the remaining tally.

; Compare the leading score digits with the active player threshold. First award is at the initial threshold, then advance by six units of the stored high-order decimal pair, increment lives and play its sound.
; Activate three ball slots by copying the primary record twice; choose distinct angles for the new copies from the split-angle table.
; Three direction/angle choices used when copying the primary ball into two extra slots.
; Walk changed-brick triples. Ignore indestructible values; use the high nibble to select six-digit points, with the special brick award scaled by stage.

; Unpacked six-digit score records. Brick high nibble selects ordinary awards; the special-brick path derives a stage-scaled record index. Exact designer scoring rationale is not required to use the records.
; Outside attract mode add six decimal digits through the source pointer into the pending tally. Preserve caller X/Y via the decimal helper.
; Sequence laser transformation tiles, changing paddle end positions until its animation terminator enables firing.
; Paddle laser transformation sequence: ordinary bytes are end tiles, $EE substitutes a middle tile, and $FF ends the transformation.
; Sequence the reverse paddle transformation, keeping catch mode if requested and restoring normal appearance at the terminator.
; Reverse paddle transformation with the same $EE middle-tile and $FF end markers.
; Move outer pieces apart, clip the full shape to the arena, and stop when the internal spacing reaches one tile.
; Move outer pieces inward until the middle and adjacent pieces coincide; retain a requested laser transformation for the next phase.
; When a capsule spawned this frame, copy its four palette bytes into the sprite-palette shadow and upload that palette.
; Seven four-color capsule palettes, selected by (capsule type-1)*4.
; Mix a sixteen-byte table, scratch seed, score digits, paddle and ball positions through adds and rotates. Return the mixed accumulator and advance the seed; carry is intentionally not normalized.
; Sixteen mixing bytes indexed by the seed low nibble in MixGameStateRandom.
; Add Y unpacked decimal digits from DecimalLeft and DecimalRight to DecimalResult, least significant first. Correct values at ten and propagate carry; preserve caller X/Y.
; Subtract Y unpacked decimal digits with borrow correction by ten. Source/result pointers may alias; preserve caller X/Y.
; Dispatch title, attract, stage setup, READY, game over and ending states. Multi-frame initializers use the substate byte and frame holds to distribute PPU work.
; Disable rendering and step through RAM reset, player/brick loading, nametable setup, palettes, HUD and playfield rendering. Reenable rendering and advance the main state when all steps finish.
; Select the active player RAM playfield and restore lives, stage, remaining bricks and timers. New stages load ROM records; attract mode selects from a bounded demo-stage list.
; The second player uses its separate playfield RAM, brick count, stage digits and enemy timers; the loading format is shared.
; Attract-stage selectors terminated by $FF; the loader wraps to the first selector.

; X is a one-based stage. Copy its 256-byte record at $C6C0+(X-1)*256 into the selected player playfield, insert the RAM layout gap, read the last byte as remaining-brick count, then append its 64 attribute bytes from $EAC0+(X-1)*64.
; Copy $DF leading cell bytes, insert the RAM gap, then resume the record tail at the adjusted destination.
; Multiply the zero-based stage index by 64 and add the ROM attribute base.
; Use stage substate to clear both nametables, restore palettes/attributes and draw the round intro text and decimal round number.
; Address/count/literal PPU commands drawing the stage-intro label.
; Restore selected player attributes, draw arena framing, scores and round digits, and synchronize life icons. Text command streams carry explicit PPU addresses.
; Literal PPU streams drawing arena framing and player/round labels. WritePPUCommandStream supplies the record grammar.

; Build 28 rows of eleven two-tile brick cells in scratch RAM, combining arena background patterns with the selected player brick-type mapping; upload them row by row. Stage 36 overlays the twelve-row DoH picture.
; Overlay nonzero brick-type tiles on the arena background; absent cells leave the background pattern intact.
; The boss picture is twelve rows of eight tiles with a sixteen-tile source stride.

; Activate the primary ball, reset its motion/speed state from stage tables and arrange six paddle pieces. An attached ball starts just above the paddle; a connected paddle peripheral supplies initial X.

; Ball speed thresholds, per-stage initial speed/top-wall adjustment and six-byte enemy spawn timers. Distinct indexed consumers establish the layouts locally; unclaimed bytes remain generic data within these bounds.
; Copy X bytes from SourcePointer to the OAM shadow; X=0 intentionally wraps through all 256 bytes.
; Copy sixteen background colors from the selected player saved stage palette into the live palette shadow.
; Select one of four sixteen-byte sprite palettes using (stage-1) modulo four.
; Four sixteen-color sprite palettes selected by stage modulo four.

; Initialize/clamp saved stage selection, accept Start or the paddle trigger, clear scores and initialize player lives. Select toggles one/two-player mode; a held button combination counts toward retaining the saved stage.
; Initialize decimal score arrays, life thresholds, mode and lives before the player intro state.
; Copy player and READY sprite templates into temporary OAM slots and select the second-player tile when needed.
; Copy player and GAME OVER sprite templates; hide the player label for single-player mode.

; Select CHR bank 1 (the second 8 KiB bank) through selector index 1 and clear nametables, restore palettes/HUD, relocate GAME OVER sprites and animate three final command streams before returning to the state dispatcher.
; Ending-return palettes, text and timed PPU command streams. Shared stream format is documented at WritePPUCommandStream.
; Hide fifteen temporary OAM entries by setting Y to $F0.
; OAM templates for player/READY/GAME OVER text. Each sprite occupies four bytes: Y,tile,attributes,X.
; Alternate player intro text streams on a thirty-frame cadence, then request stage initialization after eleven phases.
; Player-intro PPU streams with alternate visible/blank frames selected by mode and blink phase.
; Select the boss CHR bank only for stage 36. Reading then writing the same ROM table byte avoids CNROM bus-conflict corruption.
; Two CHR bank selector bytes. Reading a byte then writing it to the same CPU ROM address preserves the intended value under CNROM bus conflicts.
; Clear zero-page gameplay state from $33 onward and RAM $0100..$019F, preserving title/player/score bookkeeping.
; First reset palettes, sound, gameplay state and OAM; on the next substate clear both nametables and draw title text/attributes/HUD. Advance to title input with rendering enabled.
; Title OAM entries, palette bytes and nametable attribute data consumed by title/attract setup. These are several adjacent structures, not a single uniform record array.
; Clear nametables, load background palette/attributes and draw the story stream on the second screen. Clear saved stage selectors before scrolling.
; Select the first CHR bank, clear both screens, restore palette/attributes and draw the ending narrative stream on the second screen.
; Sixty-four nametable attribute bytes shared by narrative screens.
; Install the complete ROM OAM template using the wrapping 256-byte copy helper.
; Complete 256-byte initial OAM shadow: sixty-four Y,tile,attributes,X entries.
; Select HUD text stream for the target nametable and player mode, then draw player, high and optional second-player scores.
; HUD PPU commands for score/player labels on either nametable. Single-player streams omit the second-player label.
; Y/X supply the PPU address. Copy six decimal digits to a temporary buffer, blank leading zeroes in its first four positions, then upload and reset scroll.
; Advance vertical scroll by two pixels, clamping at $EF to prevent wrap. Use background rendering without sprites during the narrative.
; SourcePointer addresses records of PPU high byte, low byte, count and literal tile bytes. $FF high byte terminates. Y advances within the stream; each record resets scroll.
; Y/X specify the PPU start address. Fill exactly 1024 bytes with blank tile $2D, including the attribute portion, then reset scroll.
; Copy sixteen live background colors to PPU $3F00, then reset the PPU address latch to zero.
; Copy sixteen live sprite colors to PPU $3F10, then reset the PPU address latch to zero.
; A is nametable address high byte. Copy 64 bytes from SourcePointer to its $C0 attribute page, then reset scroll.
; A selects the nametable high byte. Write sixty-four zero attribute bytes at its $C0 page and reset scroll; natural callers remain unresolved.
; Additional literal tile/text command streams for title and narrative screens; record high byte $FF terminates the command stream.

; Clear changed-brick count and update up to three active 26-byte ball records. Swap each selected record into the primary working slot, run motion/collision/hit handling, then swap it back. Movement scripts may request repeated substeps.
; Rotate the active mask and swap one 26-byte record into the working slot. Swap back after every movement substep so inactive slots remain independent.
; Select a motion record from speed and angle. Load substep counts, frame delay and successive Y/X magnitudes; keep the script cursor while its repetition counters run.
; Move Y/X according to direction bits, clip top/side walls and accumulate reflection bits. Recheck the lower boundary once to preserve loss-of-ball processing.
; Direction bit 1 chooses left/right. Clip the side walls and combine the horizontal reflection with any vertical reflection.
; Convert pixel Y/X relative to $10 into an 8-pixel row and 16-pixel column plus within-cell remainders.
; Test a downward ball against the paddle and choose direction/angle from its impact segment. Reset motion timers, optionally attach under catch mode, and queue the appropriate sound.
; Paddle segments select direction and angle pairs; the impact resets the motion cursor and extends the no-hit timeout.
; Six direction/angle pairs selected by paddle impact segment.
; Skip if paddle handled the hit. Reflect direction with the accumulated axis mask, reset motion progress, and update speed/angle, including a stage-dependent top-wall speed change.
; Angle remapping bytes used after a horizontal/vertical reflection with speed changes.

; Translate selected quadrant to a brick cell, decrement its durability except $F0, clear an exhausted cell and append matching grid and PPU update triples. Update hit-based ball speed thresholds and preserve Y.
; A quadrant mask selects offsets 0,1,11,12. $F0 is indestructible; other values lose one durability count and clear when the low three bits reach zero.
; Compute PPU address from grid row/column and append a three-byte update alongside a three-byte grid-hit record. A zero replacement denotes complete removal.
; At Y >= $F0 clear this slot from the active-ball mask and reset its motion counter.
; Y/X select a brick-grid row/column. Form a pointer using eleven cells per row and return a four-bit occupancy mask for offsets 0,1,11,12; preserve Y.
; Test the working ball against each active emerged enemy. Queue points, start its explosion and choose a ball reflection axis when overlap occurs.
; Use direction and relative vertical center to select one of the two reflection axes after an enemy overlap.

; Ball motion scripts selected by speed and angle. Header gives repeat/substep/frame-delay controls; subsequent movement magnitudes occur as Y/X pairs. Direction bits are stored separately in the ball record.

; Clear hit masks and ignore stationary balls. Stage 36 uses the DoH rectangle and hit counter; ordinary stages dispatch by direction into quadrant occupancy tests, snapping grid remainders and selecting one hit cell.
; Preserve previous grid position and remainders for corner arbitration. Ignore the already-reflected axes; each direction handler produces an axis mask and exactly one selected brick quadrant.
; Direction 2 moves down/left. Axis proximity chooses an edge or corner case; the occupancy mask distinguishes isolated cells, shared edges and solid corners.
; For simultaneous grid crossings, compare previous cell/remainders and step magnitudes to decide which axis to reflect. Fully ambiguous corners reflect both axes.
; Two candidate quadrant offsets and matching hit masks for down/left corner ties.
; Handle direction 0. Check row/column edge proximity and four-cell occupancy; resolve corner ties with previous position, set reflection axes and choose the brick-hit mask.
; Resolve simultaneous row/right-column crossings; snapped remainders keep the ball on the contact edge instead of embedding it in a brick.
; Two candidate quadrant offsets and matching hit masks for down/right corner ties.
; Handle direction 3 using the complementary row/column thresholds. Resolve occupied corners by prior position and motion magnitudes, then set reflection and selected brick masks.
; Resolve the upward/leftward corner from occupancy and previous position. Some original immediate comparisons look unusual; preserve their exact behavior pending any investigation.
; Two candidate quadrant offsets and matching hit masks for up/left corner ties.
; Handle direction 1. Use lower-cell and right-cell thresholds, snap the collision position and choose a hit among occupied quadrants. Final tie handling prefers destructible cells over $F0.
; Choose a single-axis or dual-axis response for an upward/rightward corner and report the contacted quadrant for durability processing.
; Two candidate quadrant offsets and matching hit masks for up/right corner ties.
; When no capsule palette or brick update competes for PPU time, refresh the active score and high score if the tally changed.
; Draw six high-score digits at its fixed HUD position.
; Draw six first-player score digits at its fixed HUD position.
; Draw six second-player score digits at its fixed HUD position.
; Compare logical lives with drawn icons, adding or erasing two-tile icons until synchronized. Only six icons fit; extra lives remain in the logical count.
; Remove one displayed icon, then reenter life synchronization; the direct entry has a supported display contract but no known natural caller.
; Shared return after life-icon bounds checks.
; Six big-endian PPU addresses for the two-tile life icons.
; Consume the pause-text dirty flag and write either PAUSE or its replacement stream according to main state.
; Visible and cleared pause-message PPU streams.
; Alternate two three-tile gate frames every two ticks using vertical PPU increments; restore the control shadow after writing.
; Two three-tile escape-gate animation frames, written with PPU vertical increment enabled.
; Hide inactive laser pairs and write each active pair as two horizontally adjacent OAM sprites.
; Render all three ball slots or hide inactive ones. During capsule/gate overlap, alternate the primary ball between two sprite slots to control priority/flicker.
; Keep the six paddle pieces visible only in supported game states; copy their independent positions and end/middle tiles to OAM.
; Freeze in pause, otherwise advance the falling capsule and its looping tile-pair animation. Clear its type once it leaves the screen and update its two OAM entries.
; Only stage 36 uses this scheduler: spawn/move/animate hostile shots, check paddle collisions and render them during play or loss transitions.
; While the boss mouth is open, allocate one of three timed shots and choose signed Y/X velocity from paddle position. Close the mouth after the third shot.
; Paddle-X thresholds and paired signed Y/X velocities for boss projectile aim.
; For three active shots, apply signed Y/X velocity every third tick and deactivate after vertical exit.
; Advance each active shot through a $FF-terminated tile animation every five ticks.
; Boss projectile tile animation terminated by $FF; consumer wraps to index zero.
; Test each shot against expanded paddle bounds. A hit clears all active balls and boss shots, feeding the ordinary life-loss path.
; React to a changed boss hit count, queue points/sound and exchange two palette groups during the hit flash. Sixteen hits enter the timed destruction state.
; During boss destruction, blank one eight-tile strip per timed phase using the address table. After twelve strips, advance the ending transition state.
; Twelve big-endian PPU addresses, one eight-tile strip per boss-erasure phase.
; Use a 16-bit delay and mouth state to alternate open/closed PPU streams; shot allocation controls when the mouth closes again.
; Open/closed boss-mouth literal PPU command streams.
; Write three single-sprite shots to OAM, hiding inactive entries with Y=$F0.
; Outside the boss stage, schedule enemy animation, motion, spawning, explosions and OAM composition in READY or play.

; Find an inactive slot whose stage timer expired, choose a top hatch from paddle position and initialize species animation/movement pointers using stage modulo four. Hatch state 5 releases the enemy.
; Initialize the chosen enemy slot only when the hatch sequence reaches its release state.
; For three active enemies, run emergence, free movement and exit state handlers every third tick.
; Move out of the hatch, then navigate the brick grid until a clear lower area permits a scripted trajectory. Below the arena switch to vertical exit.
; Read paired signed displacement commands forward/backward; $80 reverses the script. Mirror horizontal motion at boundaries and enter exit below the arena.
; Move a departing enemy down until Y reaches $F0, then free the slot.
; Try one-pixel motion according to five navigation states. Roll back blocked axes, turn at arena/grid limits and use enemy-overlap tests plus state mixing to choose detours.
; At vertical grid crossings, test up to two overlapped cells. Return carry for a blocking brick or the upper limit.
; Check left/right limits and up to three vertically overlapped brick cells at horizontal grid crossings. Carry means blocked.
; When another enemy overlaps below, choose a sideways route or a bounded upward detour using the state mixer. Carry indicates a selected avoidance route.
; If an overlapping enemy is above this slot, turn downward; return carry only when handled.
; For overlap on the left, choose a timed upward detour.
; For overlap on the right, turn left; carry reports handling.
; Search the other two active slots for intersecting fifteen-pixel bounds. Carry reports overlap and Y identifies the other slot.
; Compute row*11+column from enemy pixel Y/X relative to $10, then add the active player playfield base into SourcePointer.
; Advance each active enemy species tile stream on its timer. $FF wraps the stream to its first tile; the first slot uses a longer cadence.
; Advance defeated enemies through the explosion tile table, with a sound on the first phase; zero terminates and hides the sprite.
; Five explosion tile phases; a zero tile terminates and frees the enemy slot.
; Draw timed three-tile hatch frames at one of two PPU addresses. A zero frame waits for spawn logic; $FF closes the sequence and resets hatch state.
; Two hatch PPU addresses followed by four-byte frames: three tiles and a delay. Zero suspends the frame; $FF ends the hatch sequence.
; Compose three 2-by-2 enemy sprites from position/tile/attribute arrays. Explosion phases change palette; odd base tiles select flipped composition.
; Species animation tile streams, trajectory displacement pairs and pointer words selected by stage modulo four. Tile streams wrap at $FF; trajectory $80 reverses traversal.
; Thirty-six 256-byte stage records, addressed from CPU $C6C0. Brick cells use an eleven-column stride; high nibble is type and low bits durability. Last record byte is the remaining-brick count.
; Thirty-six 64-byte attribute blocks selected by zero-based stage*64, appended to the selected player RAM playfield.
; Public jump entries separate APU initialization, sound selection and per-frame update from implementation.
; Reset sound selection through the sound-load path.
; A is a sound selector; tail-call the stream loader.
; Advance the sound interpreter and render APU channel state once per game tick.
; Enable channels, initialize APU registers and mark four channel notes as rests. This is a local sound-driver contract, not a hardware compatibility claim.
; Select sound zero, then enter the shared loader.
; Resolve sound selector through a pointer table. Read channel-index/pointer triples until a negative channel byte, enable selected channels and reset their duration/envelope/loop state.
; If sound loading is complete, walk four active channels through the stream interpreter, then update APU registers.
; Iterate enabled channel bits, keeping channel index and doubled pointer index separate. Decrement note durations and interpret commands when a note expires.
; Fetch the selected channel stream pointer when duration expires, interpret until a note/return and save the advanced pointer.
; Decode note bytes, optional duration bytes $80..$BF and commands >=$C0. Dispatch commands by low nibble through the sixteen-entry target table; notes apply transpose and per-channel duration.
; Continue command dispatch without advancing game time. A note sets channel duration and returns; command handlers may redirect the stream pointer and reset Y.
; Mask the command low nibble, index sixteen little-endian handler words and jump indirectly. Aliased entries share handler behavior.
; Apply note and octave transposition except for noise/rest values; initialize envelope timing and read an optional explicit note duration.
; Read envelope selector, resolve its pointer and reset envelope phase/timer before continuing the command stream.
; Read one-shot control and a following note, setting the retrigger flag before note decoding.
; Consume one byte and replace the high two control bits while preserving channel flags/volume; continue interpreting.
; Set the channel attenuation byte subtracted from envelope values before volume clipping.
; Set the packed octave/note transpose used by subsequent note decoding.
; Read repeat count and save the stream position after the operand as this channel loop start.
; Read a little-endian absolute stream address and continue there with Y reset.
; Save one return stream pointer per channel, read the destination pointer and continue there. Calls are one level deep.
; If repeat count is nonzero, decrement and jump back until exhausted. Otherwise restore the one-level return pointer if present; a missing return disables this channel.
; Restore the saved return pointer and clear its high byte so a subsequent return ends the channel.
; Clear the channel active bit and return to the per-frame sound scheduler.
; Add the consumed Y byte count to the stream pointer with carry and reset Y.
; Walk four channels and update envelope/volume, duty and pitch registers. Noise uses its low note nibble; tonal channels index the frequency table. Inactive/resting channels are silenced.
; Triangle uses its linear-counter register; other channels write the silent control value before advancing to the next channel.
; Wait for the envelope timer or read the next duration/value pair. Zero duration loops the envelope; carry reports a newly available value.
; Combine octave-base table and doubled low note nibble into the word frequency-table index.
; Little-endian pointer to the sound-command dispatch target table.
; Sixteen little-endian sound command handler addresses, selected by command low nibble. Aliases intentionally share implementations.

; Sound channel masks, note durations, octave bases, frequency words, sound selectors, envelope pointers and bytecode streams. InterpretSoundStream documents note/duration/command grammar; precise song/effect identities remain unresolved.
; Uniform trailing non-code bytes before the interrupt vectors; no structured consumer established.
; Little-endian NMI, reset and IRQ CPU addresses in hardware vector order.
; Two 8 KiB CHR banks selected through CNROM. NES pattern tiles use two bitplanes (sixteen bytes per tile); exact artwork/tile identities remain unresolved.
